choices.misconception: I added 1 to the last 9, wrote 0, and forgot to carry the 1 into the tens.
I added 1 ten instead of 1 one.
I added 1 hundred instead of 1 one.
I added 1 to the last 9 and wrote 10 in that place, so I got 19 followed by 10.

hints: When the ones go past 9 they make a new ten, and when the tens go past 9 they make a new hundred. Add the 1 to the ones and follow what happens to each place.
199 is 1 hundred, 9 tens and 9 ones. One more one makes 10 ones, which is another ten.

solutions.reliable: 199 is 1 hundred, 9 tens and 9 ones. Adding 1 makes 10 ones, which is 1 more ten. Now there are 10 tens, which is 1 more hundred. That leaves 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 0 ones: 200. The idea to keep: when a place reaches ten, it becomes 1 of the next place, and that can happen more than once.
solutions.elegant: Count on: 197, 198, 199, 200. The idea to keep: counting on past a hundred is a quick check of a carry.

whyOnTest: Place value: adding 1 to 199 makes the ones and then the tens roll over, and stopping after the first carry is the trap.
